newsitem.title: USA: Kansas City Power sees long term benefits.
newsitem.headline: Kansas City Power sees long term benefits.

text.p: Kansas City Power & Light Co, said Thursday it sees long term benefits from its merger with Western Resources Inc and recently reduced rates.

"While short-term effects of the merger costs and rate reductions were felt this quarter, the long-term benefits of our merger efforts and lower rates will be farther reaching in a competitive environment," said KCPL Chairman and President Drue Jennings in a statement.

Earlier, the utility reported a 1997 first quarter loss of about $16 million or $0.26 after making a payment of $53 million or $0.52 a share as a result of the September 1996 termination of a merger agreement with UtiliCorp United Inc .
In addition, rate reductions approved by the Missouri Public Service Commission in July 1996 lowered first quarter revenues by $11 million or $0.11 per share.

"Through the implementation of our competitive strategies, we are laying the groundwork to take advantage of the many opportunities deregulation of our industry will bring. We are taking action now to ensure our ability to compete in a deregulated environment remains strong," he said.
In February 1997, Kansas City Power agreed to combine with Western Resources in a $2 billion deal.
First quarter 1996 earnings were $24 million or $0.38.
